slides.texte_overlay:
hobbies that give you
a seriously sharp mind

writing the counter argument

once a week, write the best case against your own opinion. seeing the other side clearly makes your thinking more honest and your arguments much stronger.

going to the source

read the original study or speech instead of a summary of it. going straight to the source is slower, but you'll notice details that everyone else misses.

a daily lesson

learning one real idea a day, like a theory, an experiment or a turning point in history, slowly builds a sharp mind that sees connections everywhere.
slides.texte_sophia:
a daily lesson

i used to only read headlines. now i spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in the Sophia app, a theory or an experiment, and i see connections i never noticed before.

slides.texte_overlay:
chess puzzles

solve one chess puzzle a day with your coffee. thinking a few moves ahead trains the same calm and careful logic you'll use in every important decision.

teaching what you learn

explain one new idea a week to a friend in simple words. if you can't make it simple, you've found exactly the part you still need to understand better.
